FLASHCARD SET · AGES 4–5

Caring for Our Planet — the parent shelf: 30 cards to download and print.

The whole eco deck for printing at home: thirty caring-for-our-planet cards for ages four to five, each with its try-it job, its three pills — age, subject, level — its download button and one-tap printing; the library is the parents’ side of the class, so everything happens on this one shelf.

This is the parents’ copy of Class 47 · Caring for Our Planet: all thirty eco flashcards on one shelf, ready to print. You do not need a plan — pick the green habit your week needs most, download the card, and print it full size on A4 or Letter paper. Every card carries one try-it job underneath and four pills on top: the age it suits, the subject it teaches, the grade level to start at, and the skill it builds. The download button takes the full-resolution JPG; the print button runs a single card through your printer with nothing else on the page. There are no card pages to hop through: the shelf is the whole set.

The shelf is yours; the lesson is your child’s. The class page at Caring for Our Planet teaches each action the way a teacher would — spoken to your child, the eco job named plainly, one small thing to do today — while this wall simply holds the deck for printing. Same thirty cards, two jobs: the lesson lives in the class, the library is where parents print.

THE THREE LEVELS

Preschool, Grade 1, Grade 2.

Every card wears a level pill so tonight’s card takes one glance to choose. The levels are a suggested order, not a test — the green job your week needs most is always the right card.

  1. 01

    Preschool · Name it

    the ten cards to start with — turn it off, close the tap, plant a tree, ride a bike safely — the actions a four-year-old already owns.

  2. 02

    Grade 1 · Do it

    the ten doing cards — sort the waste, make a bird feeder, save the seeds, wash full loads — each one with a job small hands finish.

  3. 03

    Grade 2 · Own it

    the ten bigger cards — build a compost bin, restore a habitat, rescue an insect, take the train — the habits that grow with the child.

THE PLANTING SHELF · 6 CARDS

The planting shelf — seeds, shade and flowers.

Printable planting flashcards for preschool: plant a tree, plant bulbs, plant shrubs, plant a pollinator patch, collect the rain and restore a habitat — the caring-for-our-planet cards that start as seeds and end as shade, flowers and homes for wild things. Download takes the full-resolution JPG; Print runs just that one card through the printer.

THE CRITTER SHELF · 5 CARDS

The critter shelf — the bird, the bee and the worm.

Animal-care flashcards for ages 4–5: protect birds, make a bat box, make a bird feeder, make a worm farm and rescue insects — the eco cards where the child becomes the helper every small creature nearby already needs. Download takes the full-resolution JPG; Print runs just that one card through the printer.

THE RECYCLE SHELF · 6 CARDS

The recycle shelf — the sorting game.

Recycling flashcards for kids: recycle glass, metal, textiles and tubes, sort the waste and ride the bus — the caring-for-our-planet cards that turn the bins into a sorting game a four-year-old wins on day one. Download takes the full-resolution JPG; Print runs just that one card through the printer.

THE POWER-DOWN SHELF · 6 CARDS

The power-down shelf — the off-switch hunt.

Saving-energy flashcards for preschool: turn it off, turn off the heat, turn off the computer, unplug the devices, use a lunchbox and take the train — the eco cards where the off switch, the light of day and one shared ride become the child’s own superpowers. Download takes the full-resolution JPG; Print runs just that one card through the printer.

THE EVERY-DAY SHELF · 7 CARDS

The every-day shelf — small choices that add up.

Everyday eco habits for ages 4–5: close the tap, bike safely, choose wooden toys, clean your bike, eat local, save seeds and protect the trees — the caring-for-our-planet cards that ride along in every ordinary day, no special equipment needed. Download takes the full-resolution JPG; Print runs just that one card through the printer.
